Q: Does `bash` have an environment variable stack? A:

Since you are apparently fine with your sourced script creating and running a function called do_thing, you can do that, and use the local builtin to override CDPATH just until that function call returns:

function do_thing() {
  local CDPATH=

  ... rest of script ...
}

do_thing

unset -f do_thing         # don't leak do_thing itself

In other words, the stack that you're looking for is just the normal call stack.

Q: how to extract the link of the website which are using my url in their website using python? A:

you can't just crawl the web yourself to find who's linking to your site since backlinks are scattered all over the internet and not sitting in some public database waiting for you. Google search console is your free starting point, but it only shows links google's actually found and filters out the sketchy stuff, so you're definitely missing some. If you want to tap into it via python, you'll need to set up google-api-python-client with OAuth2 and a google cloud project, then query and parse what's there - totally doable but a bit of a setup. If you've got budget to throw at it, paid tools like ahrefs, semrush, or moz dig way deeper into their own crawl databases, but even they don't catch everything because each one crawls differently and hits sites on different schedules. You can grab their data using the requests library and process it in python. One more thing, if you're checking whether links actually work using requests.head(), plenty of servers will block HEAD requests or throw back weird status codes, plus they'll ghost python user agents entirely - so using requests.get() with stream=True and a short timeout is usually your more reliable move. So combine data from multiple sources like google search console and one paid API if you can swing it, and use python to dedupe and report on everything, then just accepting that no tool gives you the whole picture anyway
